title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 1 Lesson 1: Single Body SUVAT custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A car travels along a straight horizontal road at $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The driver applies the brakes, producing a constant deceleration of $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until the car comes to rest. Calculate the distance travelled by the car while braking, and the time taken to come to rest.

A sprinter starts from rest and accelerates uniformly along a straight track, covering $45\text{ m}$ in $6\text{ s}$. Calculate the acceleration of the sprinter and find their speed at the end of the $6\text{ s}$.

A stone is projected vertically upwards from ground level with an initial speed of $28\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and neglecting air resistance, find the maximum height reached by the stone above the ground.

A small ball is released from rest from the top of a tall building and falls vertically to the ground. The ball strikes the ground after $2.4\text{ s}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and ignoring air resistance, calculate the height of the building and the speed of the ball just before impact.

A train travelling along a straight horizontal track decelerates uniformly from an initial speed of $32\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to a speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a distance of $375\text{ m}$. Find the time taken by the train to travel this distance, and determine the magnitude of its deceleration.

A particle is thrown vertically upwards from horizontal ground with an initial speed of $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the two values of time $t$ at which the particle is at a height of $20\text{ m}$ above the ground.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ travels in a straight line from a fixed point $A$ to a point $C$ via an intermediate point $B$. Starting from rest at $A$, the particle accelerates uniformly at $1.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until it reaches $B$, where its speed is $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. From $B$, the particle decelerates uniformly at $1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until coming to rest at $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the distance $AB$ and the time taken by the particle to travel from $A$ to $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance $BC$ and the total time taken for the complete journey from $A$ to $C$.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from a platform that is $20\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. The ball moves freely under gravity. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height reached by the ball above the ground, and the time taken from projection to reach this maximum height.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed with which the ball strikes the ground, and the total time elapsed from the instant of projection until the ball hits the ground.

questions.prompt: A car travels with constant acceleration along a straight horizontal road. It passes three collinear markers $P$, $Q$, and $R$ in that order. The distance $PQ$ is $120\text{ m}$ and the car takes $6\text{ s}$ to travel from $P$ to $Q$. The distance $QR$ is $180\text{ m}$ and the car takes $6\text{ s}$ to travel from $Q$ to $R$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the acceleration of the car is $\frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (approximately $1.67\text{ m s}^{-2}$) and find its speed as it passes marker $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the car accelerated uniformly from rest at a starting point $O$ before reaching $P$, find the distance $OP$ and the time taken to travel from $O$ to $P$.

questions.prompt: A model rocket is launched vertically upwards from rest at ground level. Its engine provides a constant upward acceleration of $8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for the first $5\text{ s}$ of motion. At $t = 5\text{ s}$, the fuel is completely exhausted and the rocket moves vertically under gravity alone. Air resistance is negligible throughout. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed and height of the rocket above ground level at the instant the engine stops burning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum height reached by the rocket above ground level.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the total time elapsed from the instant the rocket is launched until it returns to the ground.

questions.prompt: A motorist driving along a straight horizontal road at a constant speed of $U\text{ m s}^{-1}$ observes a hazard $62\text{ m}$ directly ahead. The driver has a reaction time of $0.6\text{ s}$ during which the car continues at speed $U$. Once the brakes are applied, the car decelerates uniformly at $4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the total stopping distance of the car is given by $0.6U + \frac{U^2}{8}$, and determine the maximum speed $U$ for which the car can come to rest before reaching the hazard.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the motorist was instead travelling at $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ when observing the hazard $62\text{ m}$ ahead, calculate the speed with which the car strikes the hazard.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with speed $V\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It passes a point $A$ which is at height $h$ above the ground. The particle passes $A$ on its upward path and again $3\text{ s}$ later on its downward path. The total time that $P$ is in the air before returning to $O$ is $8\text{ s}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the initial projection speed $V$ and the maximum height reached by the particle above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the height $h$ of point $A$ above the ground, and the speed of the particle as it passes point $A$.

questions.prompt: A high-speed electric train travels between two stations, $X$ and $Y$, which are $3150\text{ m}$ apart on a straight horizontal track. The train starts from rest at $X$, accelerates uniformly at $a_1 = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until it reaches a cruising speed of $V\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It then maintains this constant speed $V$ for a period of time, before decelerating uniformly at $a_2 = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to come to rest at $Y$. The total time taken for the entire journey from $X$ to $Y$ is $125\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express the acceleration time $t_1$, the deceleration time $t_3$, and the combined distance covered while accelerating and decelerating, in terms of $V$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Form an equation in $V$, show that $V^2 - 120V + 3024 = 0$, and hence explain why the cruising speed of the train must be $V = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using $V = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the duration of the cruising period, and state the coordinates $(t, v)$ of the four vertices of the velocity-time graph for the journey from $X$ to $Y$.
